land.text: the Slovak half of Czechoslovakia: 'The national territory was divided along the existing internal borders'

predecessors.note: Wikidata Q33946 is shared with czechoslovakia, but Czechoslovakia (1918-1992) is a different state; Slovakia is its successor from 1 January 1993.

correction.text: Shape unchanged (49,241 km2); it holds from 1 January 1993, not 1992: 'Slovakia became an independent democratic state on 1 January 1993'; the infobox area is 49,035 km2

keyframe_review.note: Years only: Cliopatria starts the row in 1992, but Czechoslovakia was dissolved on 31 December 1992 ('In November, the federal parliament voted to dissolve the country officially on 31 December 1992'), so 1992 belongs to the czechoslovakia dossier (its new 1992 keyframe). Area 49,241 km2 against 49,035 km2 (ratio 1.004). The Slovak National Council declared Slovakia 'a sovereign state' on 17 July 1992 within the federation.

The same 49,241 km2 outline: the border with Czechia is the former internal boundary, settled by the 1996 treaty, whose village exchanges (Sidonie/Sidónia to Czechia, U Sabotů/Šance to Slovakia, both 1997) are far below a grid cell; no other border change appears on the pages opened.

region.text: Slovakia within the former internal boundary of Czechoslovakia

ledger.note: 1 January 1993: Slovakia becomes an independent state. 'Slovakia became an independent democratic state on 1 January 1993' after the 'Velvet Divorce'; the Slovak parliament declared sovereignty on 17 July 1992 and the Federal Assembly's Constitution Act 542 of 25 November 1992 ended Czechoslovakia on 31 December 1992 (Dissolution of Czechoslovakia page).

region.text: the Czech-Slovak frontier, where villages were exchanged under the 1996 border treaty

ledger.note: 1997: U Sabotů/Šance passes to Slovakia. The page says it was 'awarded to Slovakia in 1997' under the 1996 'Treaty between the Czech Republic and the Slovak Republic on Common Borders'; the village is too small for a grid cell, so the frontier band stands in.

region.text: the Czech-Slovak frontier, where villages were exchanged under the 1996 border treaty

ledger.note: 1997: Sidónia (Sidonie) passes to the Czech Republic. The page says it was 'awarded to the Czech Republic in 1997'; Kasárna 'remained in Slovakia'.

certainty.note: The borders follow the former Czechoslovak internal boundary and the older frontiers with Hungary, Poland, Ukraine and Austria; the Czech-Slovak line was settled by the 1996 treaty.

notes:
Slovakia, written by eu-22-g on 2026-11-01 from two pages (the Slovakia article and Dissolution of Czechoslovakia, the budget).

Wikidata Q33946 is shared with czechoslovakia in Cliopatria's table. They are different states: Czechoslovakia (dossier czechoslovakia, 1918 to 31 December 1992) and Slovakia, independent from 1 January 1993, so no merge; Slovakia is listed there as a successor. The 1992 year is the Czechoslovakia dossier's new keyframe, as for czech-republic.

The Slovakia page lists no border treaty or change since 1993 and does not cover the Gabcikovo-Nagymaros dispute; the only recorded changes are the two village exchanges of 1997, drawn as a frontier band between czech-republic and slovakia (no grid-cell effect). No ruler strip: the page names only Michal Kovac as first president. The Slovak State of 1939-1945 is not in this Cliopatria row and is not recorded here.
